newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq to export 650,000 barrels oil Tuesday - minister.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to export 650,000 barrels oil Tuesday - minister.

text.p: Iraq will export 650,000 barrels of oil on Tuesday through its pipeline to Turkey under an "oil-for-food" deal with the United Nations, Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed was quoted as saying.

Rasheed also said in a statement carried by the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) that Iraq had sent two contracts to the U.N. Secretary-General that would enable Iraq to sell its oil to international companies. The statement did not name the purchasers.
Rasheed said Iraq would give preference to Turkey in selling its oil which will pass from the Iraqi oil centre of Kirkuk by pipeline to the Turkish port of Ceyhan.
There was no immediate confirmation that oil had begun to flow.

The United Nations gave Iraq clearance on Monday to start resuming limited exports of oil, from 0501 GMT on Tuesday, to allow it to raise funds to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian items for Iraqis suffering under the impact of U.N. sanctions imposed on Iraq after its invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
